statement: Goldman Sachs forecasts top-five hyperscaler AI infrastructure spending of $1.2 trillion in 2027, up from $800 billion in 2026, a 54% jump and above the $1.1 trillion Wall Street consensus.
why: Hyperscaler capex is the single largest source of accelerator demand, and a forecast above consensus points to upward revisions rather than a plateau.

impact.mechanism: Higher planned capex at Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Oracle and Meta translates directly into accelerator, memory, facility and power orders.

evidence.excerpt: Goldman Sachs forecasts hyperscaler AI infrastructure spending will hit $1.2 trillion in 2027, up from $800 billion in 2026. This figure exceeds Wall Street consensus of $1.1 trillion for 2027.
a 54% jump in hyperscaler capital expenditures in 2027

confidence.basis: Secondary coverage of a sell-side forecast, not company guidance or a filing; forecasts are estimates rather than realized spend.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: magnitude 2 -> 3; sources: PYMNTS
entity: Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Oracle, Meta (top-5 US hyperscalers); Goldman Sachs (forecaster)
